national_raw_news.content: India and New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) comes into force on the occasion of Vijay Dashami today. The agreement will provide duty-free access for 100 per cent of Indian exports to New Zealand. Addressing a ceremony on India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement in New Delhi, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said that the agreement is aligned with the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi for Viksit Bharat 2047. He said, the agreement opens significant new opportunities for India’s exporters, particularly MSMEs, artisans, farmers and pharma. The Minister highlighted that both the countries have agreed to work towards the goal of doubling bilateral trade in goods and services with New Zealand to approximately 35 thousand crore rupees by 2030. Mr Goyal said that India’s farmers will gain wider market access for fruits, vegetables, spices and other agricultural produce. He said, the agreement will help improve productivity, support higher incomes and strengthen livelihoods. The Minister highlighted that sensitive sectors, including dairy, remain protected, keeping farmers’ welfare at the heart of the government’s approach. The Minister said that New Zealand’s commitment to facilitate 20 billion US dollars in investment into India holds immense potential to strengthen manufacturing, infrastructure, services and innovation. Mr Goyal said, this agreement will also create employment opportunities. He expressed confidence that this win-win partnership will achieve many more milestones, guided by the shared vision of growth and mutual prosperity between the two nations. The FTA between India and New Zealand was signed in April this year at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The Agreement will create new opportunities in services, investment and professional, student and youth mobility, including enhanced pathways for Indian professionals and students. India and New Zealand share longstanding and close relations, anchored in strong people-to-people ties and expanding cooperation across trade and investment, agriculture, education, sports, technology and other areas. The Bilateral merchandise trade between India and New Zealand stood at around 1.1 billion US dollars in 2025-26. The FTA represents a significant step in further strengthening these ties and creating new opportunities for businesses and communities in both countries. On the occasion, the first-ever export of a JCB machine from India to New Zealand was flagged off by Mr Goyal. Flag-offs of a range of products across the agriculture, gems and jewellery, engineering, sporting goods, footwear and leather sectors are also planned for the day. These initiatives reflect the confidence of Indian manufacturers and the opportunities the Agreement opens up for exporters across the country.

national_raw_news.title: Deepthi Jeevanji Wins Gold in Women’s 400m T20, Sets New Games Record at Asian Para Games 2026
national_raw_news.content: Indian para-athlete Deepthi Jeevanji clinched gold in the women’s 400m T20 event at the 2026 Asian Para Games, setting a new Games record with a time of 56.36 seconds today. Jeevanji’s medal marked India’s fifth gold medal and the first for Day 2 of the Para Asian Games. The Paris 2024 Paralympics bronze medallist dominated the race, finishing more than two seconds ahead of her closest competitor, Japan’s Niina Kanno, who secured silver for Japan in 58.92 seconds. Japan’s Akane Kato secured the bronze medal. Earlier today, para table tennis player Bhavina Patel secured a bronze medal after facing a 3-0 defeat to China’s Zhang Bian in the Women’s Singles Class 4-5 semi-finals. Patel, a silver medallist at the 2020 Paralympics, bowed out of the singles competition after suffering a 7-11, 5-11, 7-11 defeat to China’s Zhang Bian in the semifinals. Meanwhile, in para badminton, India’s mixed SL3-SU5 pair of Pramod Bhagat and Manisha Ramdass assured themselves of a medal by advancing to the semifinals. The duo defeated their Thai duo of Srinavakul Chanida and Teamarrom Siripong 21-15, 21-14 in straight games in the quarterfinals. Indian para archers Harvinder Singh, Bhawna, Sheetal Devi, Payal Nag, Toman Kumar and Shyam Sunder Swami advanced to the quarterfinals in their respective individual events at the 2026 Asian Para Games. Harvinder progressed in the men’s recurve event, while Bhawna advanced in the women’s recurve category.

national_raw_news.title: Home Minister Amit Shah to Visit Punjab, Meet Families of Anti-Drug Activists Killed in the State 1 hour ago 31
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah will visit Punjab today to meet with the families of anti-drug activists who recently lost their lives after raising their voices against synthetic drug traffickers in the state. This includes the recent broad daylight murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, who was shot dead in broad daylight by a chemist selling synthetic drugs when Jhota publicly opposed him in Mansa recently. Our Jalandhar correspondent reports that the body of the activist has not been cremated by his family even after a week of his murder. His father has said he will not cremate his son till justice is delivered. Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, an ex-serviceman, while welcoming the visit, has demanded a CBI probe in the case. Meanwhile, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leader and former Member of Parliament Harsimrat Kaur Badal, in a letter to the Union Home Minister, has requested to order an independent CBI probe into Jhota’s murder and the wider drug trade in the state. She has demanded an exemplary punishment for those responsible for silencing voices against drugs in Punjab. Mr Shah will also be meeting the family members of those who were allegedly killed in Gurdaspur by drug traffickers and the one, a father of a substance user, who committed suicide in Sangrur district. Later, the Home Minister is also scheduled to attend the Dussehra ceremonies in Ludhiana. Rajesh Bali/Jalandhar/Mail/0730

national_raw_news.title: Over 13,000 Police Personnel to Be Deployed Across Delhi-NCR for Dussehra Security 2 hours ago 37
national_raw_news.content: Security arrangements have been strengthened across Delhi-NCR ahead of Dussehra celebrations, with more than 13,000 police personnel set to be deployed to ensure public safety and maintain law and order. Authorities have stepped up vigilance at religious sites, crowded areas and event venues. In Gurugram, around 2,200 police personnel have been deployed at 66 Ravan Dahan venues, 17 religious processions and other related events, while 1,200 police personnel have been deployed in Faridabad to maintain law and order. Traffic police have also drawn up plans to ensure smooth traffic movement and effective crowd management. Delhi Police said personnel would be deployed round the clock at sensitive locations, while senior officers would inspect deployment sites to review security arrangements and ensure adequate manpower. Special attention will be given to crowded areas, prominent temples, pandals and venues hosting Dussehra celebrations, as authorities expect a significant turnout during the festive season. Additional Deputy Commissioner of Central District Angad Mehta said the district witnesses a substantial increase in footfall during festivals, necessitating extensive security arrangements. In Gurugram, additional police personnel have been deployed at major venues, taking into account the expected crowd size. Police have identified 12 major and 54 smaller Ravan Dahan venues across the district. Of these, 16 sites fall under the East Zone, 23 under the West Zone, seven under the South Zone and 20 under the Manesar Zone. Special security arrangements have also been made for religious processions scheduled to take place across the district. Police personnel have been deployed for three processions in the East Zone, nine in the West Zone, two in the South Zone and three in the Manesar Zone. In Faridabad, special surveillance will be maintained at event venues, markets, major thoroughfares and other crowded areas to prevent untoward incidents and ensure the peaceful celebration of Dussehra.

national_raw_news.title: Manipur Police celebrates 135th Raising Day in Imphal 19 Oct 2026 | 9:40 PM 59
national_raw_news.content: The 135th Raising Day of Manipur Police was celebrated today at 1st Battalion Manipur Rifles Parade Ground in Imphal. The celebration was attended by Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh, Speaker of Manipur Legislative Assembly- Thokchom Satyabrata Singh, Home Minister- Govindas Konthoujam, MLAs, DGP, Chief Secretary and high ranking police officers. Since 2008, Manipur Police has celebrated 19th October as the collective Raising Day of Manipur Police of the entire Manipur Police family. This year, various sports and other events were organised across the State as run-up events for the grand celebration held today. A total of 13 contingents participated in the March Past in today’s celebration while the Chief Minister presented various awards to outstanding battalions, police stations and police personnel for their exemplary performance and dedication to duty. Addressing the celebration, the Chief Minister said that around three thousand acres of illegal poppy cultivation has been destroyed, three hundred and seven cases have been registered under NDPS Act and four hundred sixty seven drug traffickers have been arrested in the last one year in the State. Shri Khemchand said that the Government is committed to combating illegal poppy cultivation and drug trafficking in the State and police and other concerned agencies have been closely monitoring the situation and intensifying efforts to identify, trace and dismantle drug networks operating across the State. The Chief Minister said that the crisis erupted on May 3, 2023 have led some youths to take up arms, however the State Government in coordination with the security force efforts to promote peace, reconciliation and a return to normalcy in the State is ongoing. He appealed to all sections of society and all political parties in the State to foster a culture of appreciating good deeds and pointing out wrongdoings with a view to rectifying them. Shri Khemchand emphasized that undue criticism would only further undermine the progress of the State and would in no way contribute to the restoration of peace in the State.

national_raw_news.title: French PM urges targeted curfews after violent weekend protests
national_raw_news.content: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said Monday that partial curfews would be introduced in some areas starting Monday evening following incidents of looting during weekend protests. At a news conference, Lecornu said he had asked French prefects to implement “a number of partial curfews as early as this evening,” describing the disorder as “very localised in urban centres.” Lecornu said a state of emergency would be declared “if necessary,” but added that curfews “appear to be more appropriate.” “There is no question of allowing the looting to become established,” he said, adding that the Interior Ministry would release a detailed map of the areas concerned during Monday afternoon, Xinhua News Agency reported. Partial unemployment measures would be activated from Tuesday for shopkeepers affected by damage and looting, Lecornu said. The government would also provide public funding to support affected businesses, he said, while stressing that such assistance “makes no sense if we are not capable of restoring order as quickly as possible.” French Trade Minister Serge Papin estimated that at least 3,000 businesses had been affected during weekend protests. Around 550,000 people took part in protests across France on Saturday. A total of 2,397 people were arrested during the protests, which were marred by violence, according to figures released by the French Interior Ministry on Sunday. A total of 997 police officers and gendarmes were injured, seven of them seriously. The police prefecture of Bouches-du-Rhone in southern France on Monday banned all gatherings and demonstrations throughout the city of Marseille from noon to 8 pm local time (1800 GMT), according to a post on X by the police prefecture. French President Emmanuel Macron has vowed legal action against those responsible for violence during protests across the country on Saturday. Tens of thousands of people flooded streets across major European cities over the weekend, venting mounting anger over surging living costs, housing shortages, and strained public services. -IANS
